svg.title: breadboard-PC: the signals of the build, from RESET to DOS
svg.desc: 1. RESET. 2. Fetching the reset vector. 3. Writing to RAM. 4. Programming the 8259 and the IVT. 5. A key is pressed. 6. IRQ1: INT 09h. 7. DOS calls the BIOS: INT 13h. 8. Burst reply.
svg.text: breadboard-PC: the signals of the build, from RESET to DOS

g.text: The bridge holds RESET high (PB2): at power-up, then for Ctrl-Alt-Del or Ctrl-\. When released, the 8088 starts at FFFF:0000 = FFFF0h, at the very top
Memory cycle (IO/M = 0): ALE latches FFFF0h into the 74LS373s. A19 = 1, so ROM CE# = NAND(A19, M) = 0; RD# reads JMP C000:0000 through the 74HC245.
The BIOS clears the RAM and puts its stack and variables at 7000:F800–FFFF. A19 = 0, so RAM CE# = NAND(/A19, M) = 0; WR# writes the byte.
OUT 20h/21h: I/O cycle (IO/M = 1), A5 = 1, so 8259 CS# = 0 (ICW1–ICW4: vectors 08h–0Fh, edge, manual EOI). Then the BIOS vectors are written to the
The bridge decodes the PS/2 frame and drops the code into port A of the 8255 (STB#). IBF and INTR go high: IR1 of the 8259, which raises INTR to the
Two INTA# pulses: the 8259 supplies vector 09h. The 8088 reads the IVT at 0000:0024 (RAM), jumps into the ROM: IN 82h (status), IN 80h (byte; 8255 CS#
IVT at 0000:004C, then the BIOS in ROM masks IR1 and sends the command: OUT 80h (OBF#), the bridge reads the byte (ACK#) and reads the sector from the
The bridge sends the 512 bytes back in a burst (STB#). The BIOS polls IBF (IN 82h), reads each byte (IN 80h) and writes it to the DOS buffer in RAM
